summary: This photodecarboxylation reaction uses direct photochemical excitation (no external photocatalyst) to achieve benzylation via triplet sensitization mechanism. The reaction is conducted at 80°C with a 78-minute residence time in an FEP capillary reactor (0.8 mm ID, 5 mL volume) using fluorescent tube irradiation and a mixed solvent system of acetone/pH 7 buffer, dichloromethane, and DMF. The flow setup employs syringe pumps at 0.25 mL/min flow rate to deliver reactants through the photoreactor. Flow chemistry dramatically improved the process by increasing yield from 45% to 77% while maintaining the same 9-hour total reaction time as batch, representing a 6.9× intensification factor. The continuous flow approach eliminated the need for multiple solvent changes required in batch processing and provided better control over reaction conditions with enhanced safety through reduced exposure to hazardous reagents.

summary: This photoredox catalysis involves a single-electron oxidation/fragmentation/cyanide trapping mechanism using Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbbpy)PF6 as the photocatalyst in methanol at 60°C. The flow system utilized a 1.34 mL photochemical reactor with visible light irradiation and achieved a 96% yield with only a 2-minute residence time. In comparison, the batch process required 3 hours to reach 93% yield under otherwise identical conditions. Flow processing provided a dramatic 90-fold intensification factor by reducing reaction time from 180 minutes to 2 minutes while simultaneously improving yield by 3 percentage points. The continuous flow approach also offered enhanced safety through reduced solvent inventory and better heat management for the photochemical transformation.

summary: This dual photoredox/nickel catalysis reaction used Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 (1 mol%) as the photocatalyst with Na2CO3 base in DME solvent. The flow process operated at 50°C with a 30-minute residence time in a HANU HX 15 oscillatory plug flow reactor (15 mL volume) using 405 nm LED irradiation and 2 bar back pressure. The reaction achieved 80% yield at 0.21 M concentration, representing a 5.3% yield improvement over batch conditions. Flow processing enabled a dramatic 12-fold intensification by reducing reaction time from 6 hours to 30 minutes and increasing concentration 21-fold (from 0.01 M to 0.21 M), while the oscillatory plug flow design provided superior mixing and light penetration for enhanced productivity (0.87 g/h).
